extracted.intended_audience: Australian Government, policymakers, stakeholders (business, academia, communities) and the Australian public interested in Productivity Commission processes
extracted.subtask_description: Operational principles and statutory guidelines describing how the Australian Productivity Commission conducts inquiries, engages with the public, reports, and frames its policy advice. Covers independence, transparency, community perspective, legislative duties and government expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Independence
rubrics_metrics.description: The PC operates under the powers, protection and guidance of its own legislation. Our independence is formally exercised under the Productivity Commission Act through the Chair, Deputy Chair and Commissioners, who are appointed by the Governor‑General for fixed periods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: We have our own budgetary allocation and permanent staff, operating at arm’s length from other government agencies. While the Government largely determines our work program, our findings and recommendations are based on our own analyses and judgments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Own budgetary allocation and arm’s‑length operation
rubrics_metrics.description: We have our own budgetary allocation and permanent staff, operating at arm’s length from other government agencies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This budgetary and staffing independence supports the Commission making findings and recommendations based on its own analyses and judgments rather than direct operational control by other agencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency
rubrics_metrics.description: Our advice to government, and the information and analysis on which it is based, are open to public scrutiny.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Our processes provide for extensive public input and feedback through hearings, workshops and other consultative forums, and through the release of interim reports and preliminary findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Community‑wide perspective
rubrics_metrics.description: We are obliged under statutory guidelines to take a broad view, encompassing the interests of the economy and community as a whole rather than just particular industries or groups.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Environmental, regional and social dimensions of our work are also carefully considered, informed by public consultation and our own research capability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence‑based analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Our work is based in evidence, underpinned by our analysis of qualitative and quantitative data, and input from businesses, academia and communities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policy advice and recommendations should be supported by both qualitative and quantitative analysis and stakeholder input.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public consultation and input
rubrics_metrics.description: Our processes provide for extensive public input and feedback through hearings, workshops and other consultative forums.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Engagement mechanisms include hearings, workshops, release of interim reports and preliminary findings to solicit feedback from stakeholders and the wider community.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting and accountability to Parliament
rubrics_metrics.description: We report formally through the Treasurer to the Australian Parliament, where our inquiry reports are tabled.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consistent with our statutory requirement to promote public understanding of policy issues, our reports and other communications activities are also directed at the wider community.

rubrics_metrics.name: Have regard to improving productivity and economic performance
rubrics_metrics.description: Under the Productivity Commission Act, we are required to have regard to the need to improve the productivity and economic performance of the economy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Have regard to reducing unnecessary regulation
rubrics_metrics.description: Under the Productivity Commission Act, we are required to have regard to the need to reduce unnecessary regulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Encourage efficient and internationally competitive industries
rubrics_metrics.description: Under the Productivity Commission Act, we are required to have regard to the need to encourage the development of efficient and internationally competitive Australian industries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Facilitate adjustment to structural change
rubrics_metrics.description: Under the Productivity Commission Act, we are required to have regard to the need to facilitate adjustment to structural change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognise interests of the community generally and those likely affected
rubrics_metrics.description: Under the Productivity Commission Act, we are required to have regard to the need to recognise the interests of the community generally and all those likely to be affected by our proposals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Promote regional employment and development
rubrics_metrics.description: Under the Productivity Commission Act, we are required to have regard to the need to promote regional employment and development.

rubrics_metrics.name: Have regard to Australia’s international commitments and trade policies of other countries
rubrics_metrics.description: Under the Productivity Commission Act, we are required to have regard to Australia’s international commitments and the trade policies of other countries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure ecologically sustainable development of Australian industry
rubrics_metrics.description: Under the Productivity Commission Act, we are required to have regard to the need to ensure Australian industry develops in ecologically sustainable ways.

rubrics_metrics.name: Take into account Government’s policy priorities
rubrics_metrics.description: The Government’s Statement of expectations (Nov 2023) asks the Commission to take into account the Government’s policy priorities when renewing and refocusing its objectives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This indicates a requirement to balance statutory independence with awareness of current government priorities when setting work program and framing advice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be responsive to changing economic environments
rubrics_metrics.description: The Government expects the Commission to be responsive to changing economic environments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commission activities and focus should be adaptable as economic conditions evolve.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enhance relationships with all Governments
rubrics_metrics.description: The Government expects the Commission to enhance its relationships with all Governments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strengthening intergovernmental engagement is an explicit expectation to improve reach and relevance of the Commission’s work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bolster external engagement and communication methods
rubrics_metrics.description: The Government expects the Commission to bolster external engagement and communication methods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This complements transparency and public consultation obligations, emphasizing improved communication channels and outreach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strengthen internal culture, capabilities and governance
rubrics_metrics.description: The Government expects the Commission to strengthen internal culture and capabilities, and organisational governance arrangements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Internal organisational improvements are an explicit performance expectation from government.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integrate performance measures into corporate plans and assess via annual reports
rubrics_metrics.description: Our corporate plans will integrate performance measures, and annual reports will assess our performance against these measures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Statement of intent (Feb 2024) commits the Commission to define performance measures and publicly report against them in annual reporting.
